title: Approval history with replay resistance and broker-level drift enforcement
objective: Introduce the first COTRA-P07 strong-approval foundation: a broker-level approval record with capability-bound nonces, short expiry, one-shot semantics, and exact digest binding, plus an append-only local approval history, so that a previous approval can never authorize a changed target and an agent cannot forge or replay approvals through its own tool or process surface. Existing per-operation digests and fresh-approval flows remain unchanged; strong user-presence (Windows Hello/WebAuthn style) remains an explicit successor.

include: broker-level approval nonce issuance bound to the exact normalized approval digest, workspace identity, and policy revision
short approval expiry with fail-closed expiration before execution
one-shot approval consumption so a recorded approval cannot authorize a second operation
exact digest binding so a recorded approval cannot authorize a changed target, command, destination, ref, or credential reference
workspace and policy revision binding so stale workspace or policy state invalidates recorded approvals
append-only local approval history recording approval id, digest, nonce, timestamps, expiry, reuse scope, decision, workspace, and policy revision without secret material
bounded local history query for audit and trust UX predecessors with redaction guarantees
agent and approval authority separation proof: no MCP approve tool, kernel denial of approve-like capabilities, and agent-spawned child processes unable to forge or replay approvals
denied and unavailable approval recording with failure-closed behavior preserved
deterministic unit and security tests for replay, expiry, digest mismatch, revision drift, double consumption, history tampering, and separation
retention of all SG-000015 local mutation, SG-000016 fetch, and SG-000017 push approval flows with no behavior change outside the broker hardening
exclude: strong user-presence approval through Windows Hello, WebAuthn, or equivalent platform verification
workspace trust creation, modification, or revocation UX
emergency revoke broadcast UX beyond the recorded decision history
changes to per-operation approval digests, prompts, or summaries
new privileged capabilities or capability families
new network, browser, UI automation, clipboard, or installer authority
approval delegation to remote or MCP callers
raw secret storage in approval records

authority_delta.filesystem: Approval history appends bounded redacted records to Cotra protected local state; workspace files, Git state, and unrelated paths gain no new writability.
authority_delta.process: No new process authority. The broker remains a local in-process decision boundary; no new executable targets.
authority_delta.network: None. Approval history and replay enforcement are strictly local with no egress.
authority_delta.ui_input: None. No new input injection or approval-surface targeting.
authority_delta.secrets: Approval records carry digests and reference ids only. Raw secrets never enter approval prompts, records, history queries, logs, or audit.
authority_delta.approval: Broker-level one-shot nonces with short expiry and exact digest binding are added. No persistent reuse and no remote delegation are introduced.

invariants: Every recorded approval binds the exact normalized digest, a fresh nonce, workspace identity, and policy revision
A recorded approval authorizes at most one operation; second consumption fails closed as replay
A recorded approval never authorizes a changed digest; target, command, destination, ref, or credential drift fails closed
Expired approvals fail closed before execution regardless of digest match
Workspace or policy revision drift invalidates recorded approvals
No MCP tool can produce, approve, or replay an approval; the kernel denies approve-like capabilities
Agent-spawned child processes receive no approval IPC handles, nonces, or secrets and cannot forge approvals
Approval records and history contain no raw secret material
Existing fresh-approval flows for file, process, Git mutation, fetch, and push keep their exact digests and post-approval revalidation
No strong-presence, trust-change, elevation, browser, UI, or generic network authority is introduced

acceptance.claim: Tests prove the broker issues a fresh unpredictable nonce per approval request and binds it to the exact prompt digest, workspace identity, and policy revision.
Tests prove expired approvals fail closed before execution even when the digest matches.
Tests prove one-shot consumption: the first execution with a recorded approval succeeds subject to existing revalidation, and any second consumption with the same record fails closed as replay.
Tests prove digest mismatch fails closed: a recorded approval never authorizes a changed target, argv, branch, ref, destination, pinned address, HEAD, prior, or credential reference.
Tests prove workspace and policy revision drift invalidate recorded approvals.
Tests prove denied and unavailable approvals are recorded as such and never authorize execution.
Tests prove the append-only history records approvals without secret material, rejects tampered records, and serves bounded redacted queries.
Tests prove agent and approval separation: no MCP approve tool exists, the kernel denies approve-like capabilities, and a restricted agent-spawned child cannot forge or replay an approval.
Tests prove all existing SG-000015, SG-000016, and SG-000017 approval flows still require fresh approval and pass their regressions with digests unchanged.
Tests prove strong user-presence approval, trust changes, persistent reuse, remote delegation, and broader process authority remain unreachable.

Exact-head Windows/Ubuntu Rust, Node, Governance, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, exact-diff security review, manual review of excluded security-sensitive files, and zero unresolved blocking review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.strong_presence: A successor grain must add strong local user-presence approval (Windows Hello/WebAuthn style where feasible) for PRIVILEGED and selected DESTRUCTIVE operations on top of this replay-resistant foundation, and must prove the agent cannot produce a valid strong approval through its own tool or input surface.
successor_requirements.trust_ux: Workspace trust management, approval history UX, and emergency revoke remain successor work and must build on the append-only history without weakening one-shot, expiry, or digest binding.

done_when: Broker-level approval nonces with short expiry and one-shot exact-digest binding are merged with an append-only redacted approval history, replay expiry mismatch drift and double-consumption tests, agent and approval separation proof, retained P06 approval regressions, and no strong-presence, trust-change, reuse, or delegation authority.

canonical_evidence.jev: PASSED: 36/36 hunks, zero findings, zero blocking findings
canonical_evidence.ocr: PASSED: Open Code Review v1.12.9 exact-range delegation, 11 files total, 10 reviewable, 1 excluded and manually reviewed
canonical_evidence.security_review: PASS on exact qualified head; broker nonces bound to exact digest workspace and policy revision with short expiry and one-shot consumption, append-only checksum-chained redacted history without summaries targets or secrets, tamper-evident loading with fail-closed consumption persistence, explicit approve-like denial through the request surface, migrated file process Git mutation fetch and push dispatch with digests unchanged and consume-before-execute, denied and unavailable recording, agent and approval separation, and retained P06 regressions
canonical_evidence.authority_boundary: Only broker-level approval nonces with short expiry, one-shot exact-digest binding, and an append-only redacted approval history are newly added. Strong user-presence approval, trust changes, persistent reuse, remote delegation, new privileged capabilities, new network browser UI clipboard installer and elevation authority, and approval bypass remain absent.
